hook: The 2-minute pre-work protocol. Lower the floor before you start.
topic: Pre-work stimulus reduction as a session-level tactic
body:
**The 2-minute pre-work protocol. Lower the floor before you start. This is the smallest effective change in the system.**

Before any work session, most people are coming from a high-stimulus state — phone, feed, conversation, commute input. They sit down to work and expect their brain to shift registers instantly. It doesn't. You bring the baseline you built in the previous 30 minutes.

The fix is a buffer. Two minutes. No input. No music, no background noise, no reading. You sit with nothing until the pull settles. You're not meditating. There is no breath focus, no technique. You're just waiting for the stimulus level to drop before introducing the work.

What this does: it lowers the bar the work has to clear to feel accessible. A quieter nervous system requires less reward signal to initiate a task. The starting friction shrinks.

It works because you're changing the comparison state, not the task. The task doesn't get easier. Your baseline drops to meet it.

Two minutes. No input. Before every session. Start there.

More in the link in bio.
